eyebrow: Cloud Operations, Observability, FinOps & Reliability · Chapter 6
subtitle: Lesson 23 · Not Just a Performance Lever

eyebrow: Most teams only use half the mechanism

steps.label: HPA / VM scale set watches load
steps.sub: adds pods or instances when a traffic spike hits

steps.label: That's the performance half
steps.sub: most teams stop there and never scale down deliberately

steps.label: Fixed capacity for the worst hour
steps.sub: pays for that worst hour 24x over, every day it isn't happening

code:
Scheduled scale-down
  -> known low-usage window (nights, weekends, staging)
  -> CronJob patches HPA minReplicas lower on schedule

Scale-to-zero
  -> genuinely on-demand workloads only
  -> dev/test envs, event-driven batch jobs
  -> accept a brief cold start on the first request
  -> WRONG setting for anything customer-facing & instant
caption: Scale-to-zero is the deepest cost lever -- and the easiest one to misuse.

eyebrow: Setting the floor without breaking reliability
titleEmphasis: but not past the recovery point

steps.label: Base the off-hours minimum on real p95 data
steps.sub: the same percentile analysis from right-sizing, not a guess

steps.label: Keep maxReplicas generous
steps.sub: a 2am spike during the 'off' window still needs to be served

steps.label: Test the transitions, not just the extremes
steps.sub: the real risk lives in scaling down and back up, not at rest

subtitle: Cleaning up the forgotten spend nobody is autoscaling.
